world.h: IRGC says it targets "violating" ships nightly
world.b: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it targets "violating" ships in the Strait of Hormuz every night, Al Jazeera reports.
world.title: IRGC targets ‘violating’ ships nightly, Trump says no attack before vote

world.h: Trump: no attack on Iran before US elections
world.b: President Trump said there will be no attack on Iran before the US elections and that talks are productive and ongoing, Al Jazeera reports.

world.h: Russian strikes kill 30 in eastern Ukraine
world.b: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine, including one on a public bus, killed 30 people and injured at least 18, as power outages worsened in Kyiv.
more: Public transport in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk was halted.

world.h: US indicts Maduro on torture charges
world.b: A new US indictment unsealed Thursday charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with conspiring to torture fellow citizens to keep his hold on power.
more: Maduro was already charged with taking part in a conspiracy to send cocaine into the US.

world.b: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in Portugal that US pressure on NATO allies to raise defense spending is not hostile, and that stronger members mean stronger deterrence.

world.h: South Korea recalls ambassador to Ukraine
world.b: South Korea will recall its ambassador to Ukraine in protest over Zelenskyy revealing a supposedly secret transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war.

world.h: Tanker hit off Qatar; casualties reported
world.b: A tanker was struck by multiple projectiles 58 miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, with casualties reported, UK Maritime Trade Operations said.
more: UKMTO reports a recent rise in attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

world.h: Spain eviction protest figure Maricarmen dies at 87
world.b: María del Carmen Abascal, the Madrid pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide housing protests in Spain, has died.
more: She died Wednesday, hours before she was set to sign a new rental agreement.
She was removed from her apartment on a stretcher last month after the investment company that owns the building raised her rent.
world.title: “She Put Her Body on the Line”: Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests

world.h: Rubio won't comment on Guilfoyle report
world.b: Secretary of State Marco Rubio refused to discuss a Wall Street Journal report that US Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle asked a Trump donor to pay a $100,000 credit card bill.
more: The report says she made the request just before her confirmation hearing, promising him access to administration officials.

world.h: Probe: accused Syrian general shielded in Lebanon
world.b: A BBC and NPR investigation found former Syrian general Bassam al-Hassan, wanted for crimes against humanity, lives in Lebanon protected and funded by U.S. and Lebanese authorities.
more: He oversaw Syria's chemical weapons program and advised Bashar al-Assad.

national.h: Mamdani: ICE agent shot man in car with child
national.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said an ICE agent shot a man in Marble Hill after agents surrounded him and a five-year-old child in his car, calling it "unconscionable."
national.title: ICE agent shoots man in car with five-year-old child in New York: Mayor

national.h: Army finds systemic failures in DC midair crash
national.b: An Army report found failures in air traffic control, helicopter routes, training and safety practices behind last year's collision of an American Airlines jet and a Black Hawk near Washington.
more: The crash into the Potomac River killed 67 people.
The report was released after months of pressure from victims' families.
national.title: Army calls for safety fixes after finding systemic failures behind DC midair collision

national.h: Christa Pike walking after failed execution
national.b: Christa Pike has begun walking and eating in a hospital a week after surviving Tennessee's attempt to execute her with lethal drugs, her attorneys said.
more: She survived two doses of pentobarbital; her lawyers say her arms were burned and blistered.
national.title: Christa Pike's attorneys say she is walking with help and eating after failed execution attempt

national.b: Gov. Brian Kemp declared a state of emergency in all 159 Georgia counties as Hurricane Isaias nears, with landfall expected near the Alabama and Florida coasts Friday evening.
more: The order bans price gouging during the storm.
national.title: Kemp issues Georgia state of emergency ahead of Hurricane Isaias

national.h: Microsoft suspended from green card program
national.b: The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft from a program to apply for green cards for H-1B visa workers, accusing the company of fraud, Vice President JD Vance said.
more: Officials also called out universities over J-1 visas and IT outsourcing firms.

national.h: House panel probes AAU over child abuse
national.b: Bipartisan leaders of the House Energy and Commerce Committee opened an inquiry into the Amateur Athletic Union's handling of child sexual abuse allegations.
more: They cited reporting by ProPublica and The Washington Post.
Chair Brett Guthrie called the reporting "deeply disturbing."
national.title: U.S. Lawmakers Launch Sexual Abuse Probe of Youth Sports Giant AAU

national.b: Isaias is the ninth named storm of the Atlantic season and the first to reach hurricane strength, after a quiet start blamed on a strong El Niño.
more: A normal season has 14 named storms, seven of them hurricanes.
Forecaster Phil Klotzbach said Isaias will still be an impactful storm for the northern Gulf.

national.h: Cornell accuser was misled on probe, lawyer says
national.b: The woman accusing several men of a 2024 gang rape at a Cornell fraternity was misled about the status of the criminal investigation, her lawyer told the AP.
more: The local district attorney decided within days not to bring a criminal case.

national.h: USS Lincoln returns after 265 days at sea
national.b: The USS Abraham Lincoln is returning to San Diego after a record 265-day deployment supporting the Iran war.
more: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave the crew the Presidential Unit Citation on Wednesday.
national.title: The long-deployed USS Lincoln is returning home to San Diego

national.h: Report: ICE used NJ warehouse as detention site
national.b: Neighbors say ICE quietly used a Roxbury, New Jersey, warehouse as a detention facility all summer, part of a billion-dollar DHS plan to hold migrants, NPR reports.

national.h: SpaceX used tourist videos to track Starship debris
national.b: Videos from cruise ships, a Club Med resort and airline passengers helped SpaceX track debris after Starship exploded over the Caribbean, an FAA report obtained by ProPublica shows.
national.title: Club Med, a Disney Cruise and an Exploding Starship: SpaceX Used Bystander Videos to Track Falling Debris

national.h: Isaias becomes first Atlantic hurricane of season
national.b: Isaias strengthened into a hurricane with 75 mph winds and is on track to make landfall between the Mississippi coast and the Florida Panhandle late Friday or early Saturday.
more: Forecasters warn of heavy rain and possible flash flooding.

national.h: Pediatricians renew call for raw milk ban
national.b: The American Academy of Pediatrics renewed its call for a nationwide ban on selling unpasteurized milk and raw dairy, citing serious risks for children, pregnant and immunocompromised people, ProPublica reports.
national.title: American Academy of Pediatrics Renews Call for Ban on Raw Milk

national.h: LA health officials target medical debt
national.b: Los Angeles County public health officials are treating medical debt like a disease to prevent, KFF Health News reports, as hospital bills crush patients.

politics.h: El-Sayed, Rogers meet in Michigan Senate debate
politics.b: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers faced off in their first televised debate in Michigan's toss-up Senate race.
politics.title: Key takeaways from US Senate debate in Michigan between El-Sayed, Rogers

politics.b: House Oversight Democrats asked Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle for financial records after a report she sought $100,000 from a Trump donor before her confirmation hearing.
more: Ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia sent the letter, obtained first by PBS News.
politics.title: Exclusive: House Democrats ask Kimberly Guilfoyle for records related to alleged pay-to-play scheme

politics.h: DNC sues Trump over taxpayer-funded ads
politics.b: The Democratic National Committee sued Trump over publicly funded TV ads it says promote his policies ahead of the Nov. 3 midterms.

politics.h: Trump to give Musk National Medal of Science
politics.b: President Trump was set to award Elon Musk the National Medal of Science on Thursday, alongside Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang and Lisa Su.
more: The awards are part of a White House summit called "Science: A New Golden Age."

politics.h: Trump pitches 'Camp David' at his Florida golf club
politics.b: Trump proposed turning his West Palm Beach golf course into a presidential retreat for his successors, calling it 'sort of a Camp David.'

international.b: The UN Security Council extended the Darfur arms embargo until December 11 but did not agree to a US plan to widen it to all of Sudan, after Russia and China objected.
international.title: UN extends Darfur arms embargo, blocks broader Sudan sanctions proposal

international.h: Police probe Sinn Fein over parade protest
international.b: Northern Ireland police contacted Sinn Fein representatives in an investigation into a protest that blocked a Protestant parade through a Catholic area, the party said.
more: The DUP, which shares power with Sinn Fein, has called for its lawmakers to be prosecuted.
international.title: Northern Ireland’s Sinn Fein faces police probe as protest tensions fester

international.h: South Korea tests first homegrown hypersonic arm
international.b: South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon, designed to fly at least five times the speed of sound, with President Lee Jae Myung attending.
more: North Korea tested its own hypersonic missile last week.

international.h: US sanctions Fiji man over China-linked bribery
international.b: The State Department designated Zhao Fugang, director of Fiji's Overseas Chinese Service Center, for paying bribes to Fijians to advance Chinese interests.

international.h: Kidnappings drain families in Nigeria's Borno
international.b: In northeastern Nigeria, families sell livestock, take loans and empty savings to pay ransoms for abducted relatives, Al Jazeera reports.
Yemen's internationally recognised government says its 'Dawn of Yemen' counteroffensive has 'neutralised' 1,860 Houthi fighters, Al Jazeera reports.

international.h: South Korea vows action on fuel exports to Russia
international.b: South Korea's foreign ministry says it will take legal action if claims by a Zelenskyy adviser of illegal fuel shipments to Russia are confirmed.

business.b: UPS is hiring more than 100,000 seasonal workers for the holiday peak, fewer than in prior years as it leans more on automation and AI.
business.title: UPS will lean on AI and seasonal workers during the holidays

business.b: A New York Fed survey found consumers' inflation expectations for the year ahead rose sharply in September to 3.9%.
more: Consumers felt better about the job market, seeing less chance of losing their job.

business.h: Stocks slide as Treasury yields hit 20-year high
business.b: Wall Street closed lower Wednesday as Treasury yields reached their highest in over 20 years and oil swung on renewed Iran war fears, Al Jazeera reports.

business.h: Florida power bills up as much as 70%
business.b: Energy bills in Florida have jumped by as much as 70% over the past 10 years, according to reporting by WUSF in Tampa.

sports.h: Dodgers beat Braves 4-1, advance to NLCS
sports.b: Andy Pages' two-run single in the seventh lifted the Dodgers past the Braves 4-1, winning the NL Division Series 3-1.
more: The Brewers are trying to close out their series against the Padres.

sports.h: Rays sweep Yankees, advance to ALCS
sports.b: Tampa Bay beat the Yankees 4-3 to win their AL Division Series 3-0 and eliminate New York.
sports.title: 2026 MLB playoff bracket: Schedule, scores as Guardians force Game 5 vs. White Sox in ALDS

sports.h: Guardians top White Sox 9-3 to stay alive
sports.b: Cleveland beat the White Sox 9-3 for Chicago's first loss of the playoffs; the White Sox lead the ALDS 2-1.

goodnews.b: Three astronauts and a cosmonaut of NASA's Crew-12 mission safely splashed down in the Pacific off Los Angeles after almost eight months at the space station.
more: The crew was commanded by NASA's Jessica Meir.

local.h: Person shot in encounter with federal agents
local.b: A person was shot during an encounter involving federal law enforcement agents in Marble Hill on Thursday afternoon, the NYPD said.
local.title: ICE agent fires 7 rounds, shoots man in neck in NYC's Marble Hill, NYPD says

local.h: Bronx exempt from Medicaid work rule
local.b: Because of high unemployment, Bronx residents will be exempt from Medicaid work requirements when new federal rules take effect in January, the state health department said.
local.title: Bronx residents will be exempt from new Medicaid work rule, state officials say

local.h: MTA chief says Byford went "full MAGA"
local.b: MTA Chair Janno Lieber accused Andy Byford, who leads Amtrak's Penn Station rebuild, of going "full MAGA."
more: President Trump took control of the project from the MTA last year.
local.title: MTA chair accuses Andy Byford, who's leading Penn Station rebuild, of going 'full MAGA'

local.h: Jersey City shakes up staff amid $255M gap
local.b: Jersey City Mayor James Solomon announced the resignations of the city's finance director and deputy mayor for housing amid a $255 million budget gap.
local.title: Jersey City mayor shakes up staff amid $255M budget gap

local.h: Man charged in fatal Queens park stabbing
local.b: Police arrested 53-year-old Abdullah Spencerel on murder charges in a fatal stabbing in Major Mark Park in Queens.
more: A witness pointed officers to him three blocks away; police are still working to identify the victim.
local.title: Bronx man arrested for allegedly stabbing Queens man to death in a public park

local.h: Data centers stir NY governor race
local.b: Gothamist's Jimmy Vielkind writes that the New York governor race pits an old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers.
local.title: NY gov race pits old immigration playbook against new outrage over data centers

local.h: Survey: NYC parents split on childcare needs
local.b: A New America survey of NYC families with young children found working parents need more weekend childcare, and most want to be the main caregiver in a child's first year.
more: Parents in higher-income areas near Manhattan more often prefer formal preschool for 2-year-olds than parents in the Bronx and parts of Queens.
local.title: NYC parents want affordable childcare. But they don't all want the same thing.

local.h: Arrest in deadly Bronx balcony push
local.b: Police arrested the man they say pushed a 23-year-old mother and their 8-month-old daughter from a Bronx balcony, killing the woman; he faces a murder charge.
local.title: Man who pushed his baby and her mother from a Bronx balcony arrested for murder, NYPD says

local.b: A 15-year-old was shot and killed and a man was wounded at NYCHA's Martin Luther King Jr. Towers in Harlem; police are questioning a teen.
local.title: Harlem community of murdered 15-year-old mourns as NYPD questions teen tied to incident

local.b: An audit questioning how millions were spent in Newark's public schools led to a referral to state prosecutors, Gothamist reports.
local.title: Audit questions how millions were spent in Newark schools. GOP says it's no surprise.

periods.text: Clear, with a low around 59. West wind around 9 mph.

periods.name: Friday
periods.text: Sunny, with a high near 71. West wind 8 to 16 mph, with gusts as high as 28 mph.

periods.name: Friday Night
periods.text: Mostly clear, with a low around 56. West wind 7 to 10 mph.

periods.name: Saturday
periods.text: Increasing clouds, with a high near 69. North wind 5 to 8 mph becoming light and variable.

periods.name: Saturday Night
periods.text: Mostly cloudy, with a low around 61. South wind 3 to 7 mph.

periods.name: Sunday
periods.text: Showers likely after 2pm.  Mostly cloudy, with a high near 68. Chance of precipitation is 60%. New precipitation amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible.
